title_en: The Coming Forth of the Mahdi
body_ar:
بعض الناس يربطون خروج المهدي بنهاية الدولة فهل هذا القول صحيح أم لا؟ و هل عليه من دليل؟

المهدي رجل من آل محمد صلى الله عليه و سلم من أهل الحجاز يصلحه الله في ليلة أي أنه لم يكن من الصالحين ولا من الملتزمين يصلحه الله في ليلة و اسمه موافق لاسم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم واسم أبيه موافق لاسم أبيه و لكنه لا يشبهه في الشكل و قد ورد فيه ألف و خمسون حديثا ألف و ستة و أربعون حديثا منها من الحديث الضعيف و أربعة أحاديث فقط هي الأحاديث الصحيحة في المهدي.

و هذا الرجل يخرج عند فتنة عند موت خليفة و قد ثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن في آخر هذه الأمة خلافة راشدة على منهج النبوة كالخلافة التي كانت في أولها و هذه الخلافة سيكون فيها اثنا عشر خليفة كلهم من قريش

و إذا حصلت الفتنة عند موت خليفة و هذه الفتنة الراجح فيها أنها أعظم فتنة على وجه الأرض ما بين خلق آدم وقيام الساعة و هي خروج المسيح الدجال فعند خروجه يموت خليفة و حينئذ يطلب الناس المهدي للبيعة في المدينة فيفر منهم إلى مكة فيدركونه بين الركن و المقام فيبايعونه و هو الذي يقاتل المسيح الدجال حتى ينزل المسيح بن مريم عليه السلام

و المسيح ابن مريم ينزل عند صلاة الفجر عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق بين مهرودتين يمينه على ملك و شماله على ملك كأنما خرج من ديماس إذا طأطأ رأسه تحدر منه مثل الجمان و إذا رفعه تقاطر لا يشك فيه اثنان لا يتمارى فيه اثنان أنه المسيح عليه السلام فيدخل المسجد و قد أقيمت الصلاة فيقولون له يا نبي الله تقدم فصل فيقول ما أقيمت لي و إمامكم منكم تكرمة لأمة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لا يحل لكافر أن يجد ريح نفسه إلا ذاب كما يذوب الملح في الماء و إن نفسه ليبلغ ما يبلغ بصره

و يدرك المسيح الدجال بباب اللد و هو مطار تَلْ آبيب الآن فيقتله هنالك و يكسر الصليب في العالم كله و يقتل الخنزير و يسقط الجزية و هذا دليل على أن الجزية سترجع في آخر الزمان في الخلافة الراشدة عند ما تفتح روما ستفرض الجزية أيضا على من لم يدخل الإسلام من الكفار و إذا فرضت عليهم الجزية فإن المسيح ابن مريم عليه السلام هو الذي يسقطها.
body_en:
Some people link the coming forth of the Mahdi to the end of the state. Is this statement correct or not? And is there any evidence for it?

The Mahdi is a man of the family of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the people of the Hijaz. God will set him right in a single night — that is, he will not have been among the righteous nor among the committed, and God will set him right in a night. His name matches the name of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his father's name matches his father's name; but he does not resemble him in form. One thousand and fifty hadiths have come down about him; one thousand and forty-six of them are weak hadiths (ḍaʿīf), and only four hadiths are the sound hadiths on the Mahdi.

This man comes forth at a trial, at the death of a caliph. It is established from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that at the end of this community there will be a rightly guided caliphate upon the method of prophethood, like the caliphate that was at its beginning; and in this caliphate there will be twelve caliphs, all of them of Quraysh.

And when the trial occurs at the death of a caliph — and the stronger view concerning this trial is that it is the greatest trial on the face of the earth between the creation of Adam and the rising of the Hour, namely the coming forth of the False Messiah — so at his coming forth a caliph dies, and at that point people seek the Mahdi for the pledge of allegiance in Medina, and he flees from them to Mecca, and they catch up with him between the Corner and the Station and pledge allegiance to him. He is the one who fights the False Messiah, until the Messiah son of Mary, peace be upon him, descends.

The Messiah son of Mary descends at the dawn prayer, at the white minaret east of Damascus, in two saffron-dyed garments, his right hand upon an angel and his left upon an angel, as though he had come out of a vaulted bath. When he lowers his head, drops like pearls run down from him, and when he raises it they fall in drops. No two will doubt about him, no two will dispute about him, that he is the Messiah, peace be upon him. He enters the mosque, and the prayer has already been called, and they say to him: 'O prophet of God, go forward and lead the prayer.' He says: 'It was not called for me; your leader is from among you' — as an honouring of the community of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is not possible for an unbeliever to catch the scent of his breath without dissolving, as salt dissolves in water; and his breath reaches as far as his sight reaches.

He overtakes the False Messiah at the gate of Ludd — which is Tel Aviv airport today — and kills him there. He breaks the cross in the whole world, and kills the swine, and abolishes the poll tax (jizyah). This is evidence that the poll tax will return at the end of time, in the rightly guided caliphate: when Rome is conquered, the poll tax will also be imposed on those of the unbelievers who have not entered Islam; and when it is imposed upon them, it is the Messiah son of Mary, peace be upon him, who abolishes it.

flags.arabic: بعض الناس يربطون خروج المهدي بنهاية الدولة فهل هذا القول صحيح أم لا؟ و هل عليه من دليل؟
flags.context: the question, which the Sheikh does not answer
options: render the question in full and leave it unanswered, as the source does
display with a note that the question asked is not the question answered
withhold until the Sheikh's office supplies the missing answer
flags.note: CRITICAL FOR DISPLAY. The questioner asks one specific thing: whether it is correct to tie the Mahdi's appearance to 'the end of the state', and whether there is evidence for it. The Sheikh gives a general account of the Mahdi and the descent of Jesus and never addresses the link, never says whether the claim is correct, and never gives or denies evidence for it. Nothing has been supplied. Published without a warning, this reads as an endorsement of the premise, which is precisely what the questioner was asking about.

flags.context: بعض الناس يربطون خروج المهدي بنهاية الدولة
options: the end of the nation-state order
flags.note: الدولة with the definite article and no further qualification. Depending on who was asking and where, this could be the Mauritanian state, a particular ruling regime, or the modern state system as such. The Arabic does not decide, and the Sheikh does not take the phrase up, so nothing can be recovered from his answer. The neutral rendering has been kept. This matters: read one way the question is political.

flags.arabic: و هو مطار تَلْ آبيب الآن
flags.context: و يدرك المسيح الدجال بباب اللد و هو مطار تَلْ آبيب الآن
options: which is Tel Aviv airport today
where Tel Aviv airport now stands
the site of the airport at Lod today
flags.note: The identification is the Sheikh's own contemporary gloss, not part of the report, and the distinction should not be lost in English. The same gloss appears in article 535 of this slice. Ludd is the town of Lydda/Lod; the airport there is today Ben Gurion airport. The Sheikh's wording has not been updated or corrected.

flags.context: ينزل عند صلاة الفجر عند المنارة البيضاء شرقي دمشق بين مهرودتين
flags.note: مهرودة is glossed in the hadith commentaries as a garment dyed with saffron or with wars, and less commonly as a torn or patched garment; the commentators disagree. The Sheikh gives no gloss. The most widely followed reading has been used and the alternatives recorded rather than a choice being concealed.

flags.arabic: و يسقط الجزية و هذا دليل على أن الجزية سترجع في آخر الزمان
flags.context: the closing inference about the poll tax
options: publish with a preface from the Sheikh's office
hold from publication pending the Sheikh's office
publish as an ordinary item in the creed series
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW ADVISED (style guide §12). The closing inference — that the poll tax will be reimposed on non-Muslims when Rome is conquered, and only then abolished by Jesus — is the Sheikh's own reasoning from the hadith, not part of the report. Stated in English without its eschatological setting it reads as a programme. It has been translated exactly as given and nothing has been added or removed.

translator_notes: Hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The Sheikh's gradings have been carried exactly: 1,050 reports on the Mahdi, of which 1,046 are weak and four sound. Compare article 527 of this slice, where he gives the same totals but describes the four differently and names Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi for one of them. Neither account has been harmonised to the other.
The long description of the descent of Jesus reproduces the wording of the hadith in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, but the Sheikh names no collection and gives no grading here. None has been supplied.

The Sheikh's own glosses inside the reports ('that is, he will not have been among the righteous'; 'which is Tel Aviv airport today') have been kept and remain distinguishable from the reported wording.
Source spellings preserved verbatim in body_ar: المسيح بن مريم without the alif of ابن alongside المسيح ابن مريم with it in the same paragraph, and تَلْ آبيب, which the source vowels.
The repetition 'no two will doubt about him, no two will dispute about him' is in the source and has been kept.
